name: Crane Company
sector: Industrials / Aerospace & defense components and process flow technologies
moat_justification: Specified-in, sole-source engineered components (aerospace sensing and fluid handling, process valves/pumps) with certification switching costs and an aftermarket annuity, proven by the filed numbers: gross margin expanded 40.3% (FY2023) to 40.7% (FY2024) to 42.2% (FY2025) and segment operating margins reached 25.0% (Aerospace & Advanced Technologies) and 21.0% (Process Flow Technologies) in FY2025, while the roic_proxy series in fundamentals.json printed 14.8% / 17.9% / 12.0% for FY2023-2025 (the FY2025 denominator is inflated by the pre-close PSI debt and escrow cash, and FY2022's 0.2% is the separation-charge year, not a through-cycle reading). That supports a moderate 6, not 7+: returns are mid-teens rather than wide-moat levels, Process Flow is tied to process-industry capex cycles, and growth is partly bought — PSI cost ~$1.15B for ~$60M of adjusted EBITDA with only a 10% ROIC targeted by year five. CAP 9.8y.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
OE_VOLATILE: OE/share range over the last 5 yrs spans >3x — normalized base helps but the business is cyclical; widen bear weight
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base

TTM capex = $53.5M - $30.3M + $25.3M = $48.5M. Corroborated by Crane's Q4 2025 earnings release Adjusted Free Cash Flow table: capital expenditures $53.5M (FY2025) / $36.6M (FY2024) against cash provided by operating activities from continuing operations of $394.8M / $257.8M.); an override never replaces a filed value — see overrides_applied and override_impact
BASE_DIVERGENCE: latest FY OE/share 5.45 vs 3-yr median 3.15 — one of them is distorted; find out which and why
WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 4.8x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
one_liner: High-quality engineered-components maker with sole-source aerospace/process positions and expanding 42.2% gross margins, moat 6/10 — but at $205.83 it clears nothing: weighted IRR 7.0% on the TTM base ($6.14/share), weighted IV@15% $68.89, and even the super-bull IV@15% ($135.58) sits below the price; it clears the 15% hurdle only below about $68.89.
exit_alert_suppressed_reason: tier exists only because of a judgment override
moat_for: Sole-source / specified-in mission-critical positions: aerospace sensing, landing-gear and fluid-handling components certified into airframes and process plants — switching means requalification
Aftermarket and repair annuity on a large installed base across commercial aerospace, defense and process industries

Pricing power in the filed numbers: gross margin 40.3% -> 40.7% -> 42.2% (FY2023-2025) and FY2025 segment operating margins of 25.0% (Aerospace & Advanced Technologies) and 21.0% (Process Flow Technologies)
Returns above the cost of capital on the post-separation perimeter: roic_proxy 14.8% / 17.9% / 12.0% (FY2023-2025, fundamentals.json)
Crane Business System operating discipline and a record backlog with raised FY2026 guidance (adjusted EPS $6.85-7.05 after Q2 2026)
moat_against: Mid-teens ROIC, not wide-moat returns: roic_proxy has not sustained 20%+ and FY2022 printed 0.2% when separation charges crushed continuing operating income to $5.3M
Process Flow Technologies rides chemical / process-industry capex cycles; Aerospace rides Boeing/Airbus build rates and defense budgets — both cyclical, neither contracted

Growth is partly bought at full prices: PSI at $1.15B for ~$390M of sales and ~$60M of adjusted EBITDA (target only 10% ROIC by year five), Trillium US pumps agreed at $240M (14.6x estimated 2026 adjusted EBITDA)
Larger diversified rivals (Parker Hannifin, Eaton, Emerson, ITT) contest the same content with greater scale
No network effects or consumer surface — the moat is qualification and installed base, which erode if programs are re-competed
